ACT-J01
As we start down and begin our descent, Grandma
points at the notches carved into the tops of the inner and
outer parapets that flank us. “Those are called crenels,”
she says, explaining that if intruders approached the wall,
soldiers could position their arrows inside the crenels and
aim from either side. We walk into one of the section’s
twenty-three watchtowers, marveling at its artfully
crafted stone archways. The history here is palpable.
When we reach the entrance to the slideway, from
over the parapet I can see people tobogganing down, the
beautiful scenery of the hillside passing them by as they
concentrate on controlling their speed and maintaining
distance from the slider in front of them. Surrounded
by all this ancient glory, the slide, built in 1998, looms
sleek and modern—not Grandma’s style at all. Instead
of suggesting we slide, I continue to follow her down,
happy with our decision to come here.
